blocks.content: The fountain in the park coughed up a thin stream of water, held it for about three seconds, then gave up entirely.

We sat on the bench by the archway. I put Winston between us. The park was quiet — pigeons, wind in the leaves, the occasional car somewhere past the trees. I closed my eyes and made myself stay still.
I'm not good at still. I've been working on it.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I was thinking this would be a good place for a story.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: The kind where two people keep almost meeting until they finally do.
That came out before I could stop it. Lena went quiet.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Or both. Those are the best ones anyway.
Across the park a little kid was chasing pigeons with total confidence — the kind you only have before you've learned that birds can simply leave.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I want a good story. That's all I meant.
I know what I have. I do. Family who would do anything for me. Friends who stay. Mornings like this one with bad coffee and a rigged claw machine and the best company I know.
I just also want someone who gets to decide — without the history, without the context, without already knowing all the complicated parts — and still chooses to stay.
That felt like too much to say out loud. So instead I stood up and said I was starving.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: It became watery. It betrayed me.
I tucked Winston under my arm and headed back through the archway. I didn't look back at the bench.
Later I'd remember it differently. But right then I was just hungry and pretending not to feel things, which is honestly one of my better skills.
